basis: The common kinds of tax-exempt organization and how the Internal Revenue Code treats each, as recalled from IRS Publications 557 (Tax-Exempt Status for Your Organization), 526 (Charitable Contributions) and 15 (Employer's Tax Guide), and the FUTA and state unemployment exclusions (IRC sections 3306(c)(8) and 3309(b)(1)); a private foundation's payout, excise and donor limit from IRC sections 4940, 4942 and 170(b)(1)(B) and the Instructions for Form 990-PF; who may hold an S corporation's shares from IRC section 1361(c)(6); not queried live. Treat as plausible defaults, not legal advice.

fields.id: Lower-snake stable key: the value an organization's tax_exempt field names.
fields.name: The status in words.
fields.code: The Internal Revenue Code section that exempts it.
fields.income_tax_exempt: Whether it pays no federal income tax on its income (true for every row here).
fields.donations_deductible: Whether a person's cash gifts to it are deductible (IRC section 170).
fields.futa: Whether it owes federal unemployment tax (FUTA) on its staff's wages.
fields.suta: Whether it owes state unemployment tax (SUTA) on its staff's wages.
fields.s_corp_holder: Whether it may hold an S corporation's shares (IRC section 1361(c)(6): 501(c)(3) organizations may).
fields.payout_pct: A private foundation's minimum payout: the share of the average value of its assets it grants out each year, by the end of the next (IRC section 4942(e)). Absent for every other status.
fields.excise_pct: A private foundation's excise on its net investment income (IRC section 4940(a)).
fields.undistributed_tax_pct: A private foundation's tax on a year's payout it still hasn't granted by the end of the next year (IRC section 4942(a)).
fields.donor_limit_pct: The share of a person's income their deductible cash gifts to it may come to, when lower than the usual 60% (IRC section 170(b)(1)(B): 30% to a private foundation).
fields.description: What kind of organization holds the status.

entries.name: Charity or nonprofit
entries.description: A public charity or other nonprofit organized for charitable, educational, scientific or literary purposes: a food bank, a shelter, a school, a museum. Gifts to it are deductible; it owes no FUTA but pays state unemployment tax.

entries.name: Church or religious organization
entries.description: A church, synagogue, mosque, temple or other religious organization, exempt without applying. Gifts to it are deductible; it owes neither FUTA nor state unemployment tax.

entries.name: Social club
entries.description: A club organized for pleasure and recreation, supported by its members' dues: a country club, a hobby or sports club, a fraternal lodge's social arm. Exempt on its members' money, but gifts to it are not deductible, and it pays unemployment taxes like any employer.

entries.name: Private foundation
entries.description: A charity funded by one family, company or founder rather than the public: a family foundation, a company's foundation. It grants out at least 5% of the average value of its assets each year, by the end of the next, last year's shortfall first; it pays 1.39% on its net investment income and 30% on a payout still ungranted a year late, both with its return on 15 May. A person deducts gifts to it up to 30% of their income.
